name: Cyrus
role: King of Persia who let the exiles go home
whenBasis: The reign as the rulers' data dates it, from sources outside the Bible.
summary: King of Persia whose first-year proclamation ends Chronicles and opens Ezra: the LORD, the God of heaven, had appointed him to build a house at Jerusalem, and any of His people might go up. He gave back the temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken. Isaiah names him the LORD's shepherd and His anointed, whose right hand He had grasped to subdue nations.
body: Ezra says the LORD stirred his spirit to fulfil the word spoken through Jeremiah. When the rebuilding was challenged under Darius, a memorandum of his decree was found at Ecbatana, giving the temple's dimensions and paying its costs from the royal treasury.
Daniel is said to have remained until his first year, and dates his last vision to Cyrus's third year.

moments.text: Daniel's vision in his third year

later.text: The Cyrus Cylinder, found at Babylon in 1879, is his own account of taking Babylon without a battle and returning the gods of other cities, and their peoples, to their homes. It does not mention the Jews.
The Nabonidus Chronicle records that Babylon fell to his army without a battle in 539 BC and that Cyrus entered it days later.
His tomb stands at Pasargadae in Iran.
